###current incompatibility between Seurat v5 + ggplot2 4.0.x; downgrading ggplot2 as suggested by Seurat team
```{r}
remove.packages("ggplot2")
remotes::install_version("ggplot2", version = "3.5.2")
packageVersion("ggplot2")
install.packages("patchwork")
```

```{r}
plot <- DimPlot(
  mac.TX, 
  reduction = "umap", 
  order = FALSE, 
  group.by = "renamed_clusters", 
  raster = FALSE, 
  label = FALSE, 
  pt.size = 1.2, 
  cols = colors
) +
scale_x_continuous(name="UMAP 1") +
scale_y_continuous(name="UMAP 2") +
scale_color_manual(
  breaks = c("1", "2", "3", "4H", "4I", "4C", "4R"),  
  labels = c("1: Monocyte-like", "2: MHCII+", "3: sNaM", "4H: Homeostatic", "4I: Inflammatory", "4C: Ctsk+", "4R: Regulatory"),
  values=colors) +
theme(
  strip.text.x = element_text(size = 18, face = "plain"),
  plot.title = element_blank()
)

umap_coords <- as.data.frame(Embeddings(mac.TX, reduction = "umap"))
umap_coords$cluster <- mac.TX$renamed_clusters
umap_coords$renamed_clusters <- mac.TX$renamed_clusters


# Compute the median center (or any other appropriate summary) for each cluster within each facet
cluster_centers <- umap_coords %>%
  group_by(renamed_clusters, cluster) %>%
  summarize(umap_1 = median(umap_1), 
            umap_2 = median(umap_2), 
            .groups = 'drop')

plot <- plot + 
  geom_point(data = cluster_centers, 
             aes(x = umap_1, y = umap_2), 
             shape = 21,     
             fill = scales::alpha("white", 0.6),  
             color = "transparent", 
             size = 8)        

plot <- plot +
  geom_text(data = cluster_centers,
            aes(x = umap_1, y = umap_2, label = cluster),
            fontface = "plain",
            size = 5)

plot
ggsave(paste0(dir, "/Clusters_UMAP.png"), plot = plot, height = 5, width = 6, dpi = 600)
```

#DotPlot
```{r}
mac.TX$renamed_clusters <- factor(mac.TX$renamed_clusters,
                                         levels = c("1", "2", "3", "4H", "4I", "4C", "4R"))

# Set the active identity if needed
Idents(mac.TX) <- mac.TX$renamed_clusters

levels(Idents(mac.TX))

genes2 <- c(
  "Gpnmb", "Abcg1", "Ly6c2", "Thbs1",  #1
  "Csf2rb", "Cd74", "Lyz1", #2
  "Cd9", "Pdgfb", "Cx3cr1", #3
  "Gdf15", "Mat2a", #4H
  "Il1a", "Cxcl1", "Ccl4", #4I
  "Ctsk", "Cd109", #4C
  "Csf1r",  "Fos", "Maf", "Jun" #4R
  )


generate_dotplot <- function(seurat_object, features, object_name) {
  # Convert feature names to italic expression
  features_italic <- lapply(features, function(x) bquote(italic(.(x))))
  
  plot <- DotPlot(seurat_object, features = features, scale = TRUE, cols = c("RdYlBu")) + 
    geom_point(aes(size = pct.exp), shape = 21, colour = "black", stroke = 0.5) +
    guides(size = guide_legend(override.aes = list(shape = 21, colour = "black", fill = "white"), title = "Percent Expression")) +
    xlab('') +  
    ylab('Cluster') +
    RotatedAxis() +
    scale_y_discrete(limits = rev(levels(Idents(seurat_object)))) + 
    scale_x_discrete(labels = features_italic) +  
    theme(axis.text.y = element_text(color = colors.rev, size = 14, face = "bold"),
          axis.title = element_text(size = 14),
          panel.background = element_blank(),
          panel.border = element_rect(fill = NA),
          text = element_text(size = 12),
          panel.grid.major.x = element_line(color = "grey80"),
          panel.grid.major.y = element_line(color = "grey80"))
  
  filename <- paste0(dir, "/", object_name, "_", paste(head(features), collapse = "_"), "_dotplot.png")
  
  ggsave(filename, plot = plot, height = 3.8, width = 2.6 + length(features) * 0.2, dpi = 600)
  
  return(filename)
}


generate_dotplot(mac.TX, genes2, "TX_reference_mapped")


```

#visualization of adaptation genes

```{r}
D16_4_filtered <- read.xlsx("Results/3TXFindMarkers/TX.markers.D16_4_filtered.xlsx")

genes_adaptation <- c(
  "Csf1r", "Fgfr1", "Cd209d", "Clec10a", "Tnfrsf12a",
  "Ccl2", "Hbegf", "Ctsk", "Serpinb6a", "Timp2",
  "Klf4", "Maf", "Notch1", "Fosb", "Igf1",
  "Csf2rb", "Cd86", "Ptprc", "Ptgs2", "Ccr2", "Thbs1"
)

generate_experiment_dotplot <- function(seurat_object, marker_table, features, object_name) {
  # check marker table has Gene column
  if (!"Gene" %in% colnames(marker_table)) {
    stop("marker_table must contain a column named 'Gene'.")
  }
  
  # keep requested genes that are present in marker table
  genes_present <- features[features %in% marker_table$Gene]
  genes_missing <- setdiff(features, genes_present)
  
  if (length(genes_missing) > 0) {
    warning(
      "These genes are not present in marker_table: ",
      paste(genes_missing, collapse = ", ")
    )
  }
  
  if (length(genes_present) == 0) {
    stop("None of the selected genes are present in marker_table.")
  }
  
  # also make sure genes exist in the Seurat object
  genes_present <- genes_present[genes_present %in% rownames(seurat_object)]
  
  if (length(genes_present) == 0) {
    stop("None of the selected genes are present in the Seurat object.")
  }
  
  # set experiment order explicitly
  seurat_object$Experiment <- factor(
    seurat_object$Experiment,
    levels = c("D4", "R4", "D16", "R16")
  )
  Idents(seurat_object) <- "Experiment"
  
  # italic labels
  features_italic <- lapply(genes_present, function(x) bquote(italic(.(x))))
  
  p <- DotPlot(
    seurat_object,
    features = genes_present,
    group.by = "Experiment",
    scale = TRUE,
    cols = "RdYlBu"
  ) +
    geom_point(aes(size = pct.exp), shape = 21, colour = "black", stroke = 0.5) +
    guides(
      size = guide_legend(
        override.aes = list(shape = 21, colour = "black", fill = "white"),
        title = "Percent Expression"
      )
    ) +
    xlab("") +
    ylab("") +
    RotatedAxis() +
    scale_y_discrete(limits = c("D4", "D16", "R4", "R16")) +
    scale_x_discrete(labels = features_italic) +
    theme(
      axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
      axis.title = element_text(size = 14),
      panel.background = element_blank(),
      panel.border = element_rect(fill = NA),
      text = element_text(size = 12),
      panel.grid.major.x = element_line(color = "grey80"),
      panel.grid.major.y = element_line(color = "grey80")
    )
  
  filename <- paste0(dir, "/", object_name, "_dotplot.png")
  
  ggsave(
    filename = filename,
    plot = p,
    width = 2.8 + length(genes_present) * 0.22,
    height = 3.8,
    dpi = 600
  )
  
  return(p)
}

p_adapt <- generate_experiment_dotplot(
  seurat_object = mac.TX,
  marker_table = D16_4_filtered,
  features = genes_adaptation,
  object_name = "D16_4_adaptation_genes"
)

p_adapt
```


#cluster origin split by timepoint
```{r}

# Ensure experiment order
mac.TX$Experiment <- factor(mac.TX$Experiment, levels = c("D4", "R4", "D16", "R16"))

# Colors mapped to Experiment levels (named for easy subsetting)
cols <- c("D4"="#0000FF", "R4"="#55A0FB", "D16"="#0000FF", "R16"="#55A0FB")

# Nice labels for legend
lab_map <- c("D4"="BM-mac",
             "R4"="Res-mac",
             "D16"="BM-mac",
             "R16"="Res-mac")

# Pull metadata
meta <- mac.TX@meta.data

# Helper to make a fractional stacked bar for a subset of experiments
make_plot <- function(exps, title){
  df <- meta %>%
    filter(Experiment %in% exps) %>%
    count(renamed_clusters, Experiment, name = "n") %>%
    group_by(renamed_clusters) %>%
    mutate(frac = n / sum(n)) %>%
    ungroup()

  ggplot(df, aes(x = renamed_clusters, y = frac, fill = Experiment)) +
    geom_col() +
    scale_fill_manual(values = cols[exps], breaks = exps, labels = lab_map[exps], name = "") +
    labs(title = title, x = "Cluster", y = "Fraction of cells") +
    scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.02))) +
    theme_classic(base_size = 11) +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
}

p_4   <- make_plot(c("D4","R4"),   "")
p_16  <- make_plot(c("D16","R16"), "")

# Combine plots; share one legend at the bottom
combined <- p_4 + p_16 + plot_layout(guides = "collect") & theme(legend.position = "bottom")
print(combined)

# Save combined figure
ggsave(paste0(dir, "/Cluster_origin_split.png"), combined, dpi = 600, height = 4, width = 4)

```





















#### rename clusters - probably needs to be removed
```{r}
table(mac.TX$predicted.new_clusters)

# 1. Define the mapping vector
cluster_mapping <- c("1" = "4H", 
                     "2" = "4I", 
                     "3" = "2", 
                     "4" = "4R", 
                     "5" = "4C", 
                     "6" = "1", 
                     "7" = "3")

# 2. Extract the predicted clusters from the meta.data slot
# This ensures you work with the correct ordering and cell names.
predicted <- as.character(mac.TX@meta.data$predicted.new_clusters)

# Map the predicted clusters to new labels using the mapping vector
new_metadata <- cluster_mapping[predicted]

# 3. Assign the names of the new metadata vector to be the Seurat cell names.
names(new_metadata) <- rownames(mac.TX@meta.data)

# Optionally check the head to verify the names are now cell barcodes:
head(new_metadata)

# 4. Add the new metadata column to the Seurat object with AddMetaData()
mac.TX <- AddMetaData(mac.TX, metadata = new_metadata, col.name = "renamed_clusters")

# Verify that the column was correctly added:
table(mac.TX$renamed_clusters)

mac.TX$renamed_clusters <- factor(mac.TX$renamed_clusters, 
                                levels = c("1", "2", "3", "4H", "4I", "4C", "4R"))

Idents(mac.TX) <- mac.TX$renamed_clusters
```
